components.note: 弓 (bow) — 弹 relates to a projectile shot from a bow, like a pellet
单 (dān) gives a loose sound connection to 弹's reading dàn
艹 (grass/plant) — many traditional medicines were made from plants and herbs
约 (yuē) gives a sound related to 药's reading yào, from an older, closer pronunciation link

example.hanzi: 士兵们检查了弹药的库存。
example.pinyin: Shìbīngmen jiǎnchále dànyào de kùcún.
example.english: The soldiers checked the ammunition inventory.
example.fact: Gunpowder, invented in China during the 9th century by Daoist alchemists searching for an elixir of immortality, was originally used for fireworks and only later adapted for weapons — one of history's more ironic technological accidents.

components.note: 土 (earth) — 坠 describes something falling down toward the ground.
队 (duì) gives a sound distantly related to zhuì, sharing the rhyme -uì but the initial consonant has drifted over time.
入 depicts a simple wedge or arrow shape pointing inward, showing the direction of entering.

example.hanzi: 那颗小行星最终坠入了地球的大气层。
example.pinyin: Nà kē xiǎoxíngxīng zuìzhōng zhuìrùle Dìqiú de dàqìcéng.
example.english: That asteroid eventually fell into Earth's atmosphere.
example.fact: Roughly 48.5 tons of meteoritic material fall into Earth's atmosphere every day, according to NASA estimates — almost all of it burns up as harmless streaks of light before ever reaching the ground.

components.note: 山 (mountain) surrounds the character, setting the scene.
幺 (small, doubled here) shows tiny hidden niches within the mountainside, giving 幽 its meaning 'secluded, hidden, dark.'
黑 (black/dark) pictures nightfall.
犬 (dog) pictures a dog keeping silent watch in the dark, giving 默 its meaning 'silent, still.'
咸 (all, together) — 感 relates to a shared reaction.
心 (heart) — feelings that stir the heart gave 感 its meaning 'to feel' or 'emotion.'

example.hanzi: 他的幽默感让整个办公室都轻松起来。
example.pinyin: Tā de yōumògǎn ràng zhěnggè bàngōngshì dōu qīngsōng qǐlái.
example.english: His sense of humor lightened up the whole office.
example.fact: Laughter triggers the release of endorphins in the brain and can measurably lower levels of the stress hormone cortisol — researchers at Loma Linda University found that even anticipating a funny event produces beneficial changes in mood-related brain chemistry before the laughter even starts.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 停 relates to a person coming to a halt
亭 (tíng) gives the sound — an exact match with 停's reading tíng
电 (simplified from 電) depicts a bolt of lightning — since lightning is a natural form of electricity, the character came to mean 'electricity.'

example.hanzi: 台风过后,整座城市停电了三天。
example.pinyin: Táifēng guòhòu, zhěng zuò chéngshì tíngdiànle sān tiān.
example.english: After the typhoon, the whole city lost power for three days.
example.fact: The largest blackout in history struck India in July 2012, cutting power to roughly 620 million people — about 9% of the world's population at the time — after a cascading grid failure across northern and eastern states.

meanings: (basketball, soccer etc) to get past an opponent

components.note: 辶 (to walk/move) — shows 过's core meaning of 'passing through' or 'crossing'
咼 (guō) gives a sound close to 过's reading guò; the simplified form 过 now uses 寸 in place of 咼, but the phonetic connection traces back to the traditional character 過
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.

example.hanzi: 他用一个漂亮的过人动作晃过了后卫。
example.pinyin: Tā yòng yī gè piàoliang de guòrén dòngzuò huàngguòle hòuwèi.
example.english: He beat the defender with a beautiful dribbling move.
example.fact: Elite soccer players can react to a sudden change in the ball's direction in under 200 milliseconds, faster than the conscious brain can fully process the decision — much of that split-second footwork is thought to rely on trained reflexive circuits rather than deliberate thought.

components.note: 日 (sun/day) — relates to 时's meaning of 'time, season'; the phonetic part of the character was later replaced by 寸 in the simplified form
The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'
日 (sun/day) — relates to 时's meaning of 'time, season'; the phonetic part of the character was later replaced by 寸 in the simplified form

example.hanzi: 她时不时会想起在巴黎度过的那个夏天。
example.pinyin: Tā shíbùshí huì xiǎngqǐ zài Bālí dùguò de nàge xiàtiān.
example.english: She thinks from time to time about that summer spent in Paris.
example.fact: Autobiographical memories tend to cluster disproportionately around ages 15 to 25, a phenomenon psychologists call the 'reminiscence bump' — one leading explanation is that identity-forming experiences during that window get encoded more richly and are recalled more often throughout life.

components.note: 火 (fire) — flame at the heart of the picture.
暴 (violent, sudden) — a burst of intense fire, together giving 爆 its meaning 'to explode, burst.'
米 depicts scattered grains of husked rice around a central stalk — a simple picture giving 米 its meaning 'rice, grain.'
艹 (plant) — the living thing in bloom.
化 (transformation) — the plant changing into blossom, the source of 花's meaning 'flower.'

example.hanzi: 电影开始前,他买了一大桶爆米花。
example.pinyin: Diànyǐng kāishǐ qián, tā mǎile yī dà tǒng bàomǐhuā.
example.english: Before the movie started, he bought a large tub of popcorn.
example.fact: Popcorn kernels pop because each one traps a small amount of water inside a hard hull; when heated past about 180°C, the water flashes into steam and the pressure buildup ruptures the hull explosively, turning the starch inside into the familiar fluffy puff.

components.note: 艹 (grass) — 莎 originally named a type of sedge grass.
沙 (shā) gives the sound — an exact match with 莎.
士 is traditionally read as a picture of a battle-axe or ceremonial blade, a symbol once carried by men of standing — the origin of its meaning 'gentleman, scholar-official, soldier.'
比 is made of two identical 匕 (spoon) shapes placed side by side — comparing two similar things led to its meaning 'to compare.'
A pictograph of a cross-shaped building, possibly an altar or temple floor plan; the character was later adopted to write 'Asia' (亚洲) and the unrelated meaning 'second, next.'

example.hanzi: 莎士比亚一生创作了三十多部戏剧。
example.pinyin: Shāshìbǐyà yīshēng chuàngzuòle sānshí duō bù xìjù.
example.english: Shakespeare wrote more than thirty plays in his lifetime.
example.fact: No one is certain how William Shakespeare spelled his own name — surviving signatures show variants like 'Shakspere' and 'Shaksper,' since standardized spelling didn't exist in Elizabethan England and even his own family disagreed on it.

components.note: 用 is thought to picture a wooden bucket or pail, an everyday tool — its practical role in daily life gave rise to the meaning 'to use, to employ.'
力 depicts the blade of a plow — since plowing fields took great physical effort, the shape came to represent strength or power.

example.hanzi: 他用力一推,门终于开了。
example.pinyin: Tā yònglì yī tuī, mén zhōngyú kāile.
example.english: He pushed hard, and the door finally opened.
example.fact: The strongest documented human jaw bite force, measured in laboratory tests on the molars, has reached over 4,300 newtons — more than four times an average human bite, though still far below a saltwater crocodile's roughly 16,000 newtons.

meanings: (before a number) to be less than

components.note: The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'
氵 (water) — relates to 满's meaning 'full,' water filling to the brim.
㒼 (mán) gives a sound hint — 满 is pronounced mǎn, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 员工们对新政策表示不满。
example.pinyin: Yuángōngmen duì xīn zhèngcè biǎoshì bùmǎn.
example.english: The employees expressed dissatisfaction with the new policy.
example.fact: Gallup's long-running State of the Global Workplace survey has repeatedly found that only about one in five employees worldwide report feeling engaged at work, a pattern that has held remarkably steady across most years the survey has run since 2009.

components.note: 扌 (hand) shows 揭 relates to an action done by hand, like lifting a cover off.
曷 (hé) gives a sound distantly related to jiē, having drifted apart over time.
雨 (rain) — 露 names a form of moisture related to weather.
路 (lù) gives the sound — an exact match with 露.

example.hanzi: 记者揭露了这家公司的财务造假。
example.pinyin: Jìzhě jiēlùle zhè jiā gōngsī de cáiwù zàojiǎ.
example.english: The journalist exposed the company's financial fraud.
example.fact: The Watergate scandal that led to President Nixon's 1974 resignation was uncovered largely through the reporting of two Washington Post journalists, Bob Woodward and Carl Bernstein, whose key source inside the FBI was kept anonymous as 'Deep Throat' for over 30 years until his identity was revealed in 2005.

components.note: 穴 (a cave/hole) — the den the dog bursts from.
犬 (dog) — a dog suddenly darting out of its den gave 突 its meaning 'sudden, abrupt.'
屮 (a young sprout) growing up and out of 凵 (a container or pit) — a picture of something emerging, hence 'going out.'

example.hanzi: 这座山峰在云层中显得格外突出。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò shānfēng zài yúncéng zhōng xiǎnde géwài tūchū.
example.english: This mountain peak stands out remarkably above the clouds.
example.fact: Mount Everest's summit is the highest point above sea level, but measured from base to peak, Mauna Kea in Hawaii is taller overall — over 10,000 meters when the portion submerged below the Pacific Ocean floor is included.

components.note: 辛 (bitter/pungent) — 辣 describes a pungent, spicy taste.
束 (shù) gives a sound only distantly related to là today, having drifted apart over time.
木 (wood, tree) — 椒 (pepper, spice) is a plant/tree product.
叔 (shū) gives a sound only distantly related to jiāo today, a connection that has faded over roughly three millennia of sound change.

example.hanzi: 她做的川菜放了很多辣椒。
example.pinyin: Tā zuò de Chuāncài fàngle hěnduō làjiāo.
example.english: The Sichuan dish she made had a lot of chili peppers in it.
example.fact: The compound capsaicin, responsible for chili peppers' heat, doesn't actually burn tissue — it binds to the same heat-sensing receptors that detect genuinely hot temperatures, tricking the nervous system into registering pain and warmth that isn't really there.

components.note: 米 (grain) — 粉 names a fine powder, originally made by grinding grain.
分 (fēn) gives a sound very close to fěn, sharing the initial and rhyme — only the tone differs.
⺈ (a person, bent over) — the figure whose outward expression is being depicted.
巴 — traditionally linked to desire or emotion, so together the character points to a person's expression or complexion, extended to 色's meaning 'color, appearance.'

example.hanzi: 她最喜欢的颜色是粉色。
example.pinyin: Tā zuì xǐhuan de yánsè shì fěnsè.
example.english: Her favorite color is pink.
example.fact: The idea that pink is inherently a girl's color is a fairly recent Western convention — as late as the early 20th century, American parenting guides sometimes recommended pink for boys as the stronger, more dramatic color and blue for girls as delicate and dainty, before the association flipped by the mid-1900s.

components.note: 亲 (here representing a tree, related to 榛/hazel) — 新 pictures a tree being cut.
斤 (an axe) — freshly chopping wood gave 新 its meaning of something 'new' or 'fresh.'
屮 (a young shoot) growing up out of 土 (earth/soil) — a picture of new life emerging from the ground.

example.hanzi: 医院里传来了一个新生儿的哭声。
example.pinyin: Yīyuàn lǐ chuánláile yī gè xīnshēng'ér de kūshēng.
example.english: The cry of a newborn baby echoed through the hospital.
example.fact: A human newborn's brain is only about 25% of its eventual adult size at birth, compared to roughly 90% for a newborn chimpanzee — this extended period of external brain growth is one reason human infancy is so much longer and more dependent than in other primates.

components.note: 辛 is traditionally read as a picture of a hot branding iron, once used to mark prisoners — a harsh origin behind its meaning 'bitter, laborious.'
並 (side by side, together) — represents everyone, all people.
日 (sun) — everyone standing together under the same sun gave 普 its meaning 'universal, general, widespread.'
木 (tree) is repeated three times, piling up to picture a dense forest.

example.hanzi: 他姓辛普森,是我们公司的新经理。
example.pinyin: Tā xìng Xīnpǔsēn, shì wǒmen gōngsī de xīn jīnglǐ.
example.english: His surname is Simpson; he's our company's new manager.
example.fact: The animated sitcom The Simpsons has run for over 35 seasons since 1989, making it the longest-running scripted primetime series in American television history, surpassing even long-running dramas and sketch shows by a wide margin.

components.note: 皿 (dish) — 盛 relates to filling a dish or vessel to abundance.
成 (chéng) gives a sound distantly related to shèng, having drifted apart over time.
A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'

example.hanzi: 奥运会开幕式是一场盛大的表演。
example.pinyin: Àoyùnhuì kāimùshì shì yī chǎng shèngdà de biǎoyǎn.
example.english: The Olympic opening ceremony was a grand performance.
example.fact: The 2008 Beijing Olympics opening ceremony reportedly cost around $100 million to produce and involved more than 15,000 performers, choreographed in part using massive LED floor panels that were, at the time, among the largest ever built for a live event.

components.note: A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'
土 (earth/soil) — 地's original meaning is 'earth, ground'
也 (yě) gives a partial sound match for 地's other reading dì; in this grammatical-particle usage the character is instead pronounced 'de'

example.hanzi: 春天来了,大地重新披上了绿装。
example.pinyin: Chūntiān láile, dàdì chóngxīn pīshàngle lǜzhuāng.
example.english: Spring has arrived, and the earth is dressed in green again.
example.fact: Roughly 71% of Earth's surface is covered by ocean, meaning the solid ground usually pictured when thinking of 'the earth' is really the minority terrain of the planet.

components.note: 辶 (walking/movement) — relates to 近's meaning 'near, close,' a short distance to walk.
斤 (jīn) gives a sound hint — 近 is pronounced jìn, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.
Originally depicted a wheat plant; this agricultural picture was borrowed early on to represent the unrelated verb 'to come.'

example.hanzi: 近来天气变化很大。
example.pinyin: Jìnlái tiānqì biànhuà hěn dà.
example.english: The weather has changed a lot recently.
example.fact: 2023 and 2024 were both confirmed by NASA and NOAA as the warmest years in the modern instrumental temperature record, each surpassing the previous record within just a year of each other.

components.note: 夕 (evening/night), doubled — two nights stacked together suggested the idea of accumulation, giving 多 its meaning of 'many, much.'
干 (originally a person) shown carrying a heavy load of grain on their back — since harvests came once a year, the character came to mean 'year.'

example.hanzi: 他们多年来一直保持联系。
example.pinyin: Tāmen duōnián lái yīzhí bǎochí liánxì.
example.english: They've stayed in touch for many years.
example.fact: The University of Queensland's Pitch Drop Experiment, begun in 1927, is the world's longest continuously running laboratory experiment — the tar-like pitch inside is so viscous that only nine drops have fallen in nearly a century, and no one has ever witnessed a drop actually fall in real time.

meanings: to be familiar with the situation

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 知 relates to speaking what one knows.
矢 (shǐ) gives a hint of the sound — 知 is pronounced zhī, a connection that has faded over time.
忄 (heart) — 情 relates to feelings and emotions.
青 (qīng) gives the sound — 情 is pronounced qíng, a close match differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 只有少数高层知情这项计划。
example.pinyin: Zhǐyǒu shǎoshù gāocéng zhīqíng zhè xiàng jìhuà.
example.english: Only a few senior executives knew the details of this plan.
example.fact: During the Manhattan Project, information was so tightly compartmentalized that most of the roughly 130,000 people who worked on it, including many scientists, had no idea they were helping build an atomic bomb until it was used in 1945.

components.note: Originally depicted a wheat plant; this agricultural picture was borrowed early on to represent the unrelated verb 'to come.'
回 depicts a spiral or winding shape — something that turns back on itself, giving rise to the meaning 'to return.'

example.hanzi: 他每天来回于家和公司之间。
example.pinyin: Tā měitiān láihuí yú jiā hé gōngsī zhījiān.
example.english: He commutes back and forth between home and the office every day.
example.fact: The average American commuter spends roughly 27 minutes traveling to work one way, adding up to about 224 hours — nearly nine full days — spent commuting over the course of a year, according to U.S. Census Bureau data.

components.note: 囗 (an enclosure or boundary) frames the scene.
大 (a person, arms outstretched) resting inside the enclosure — reclining within a fixed boundary suggested reliance on something, giving 因 its meaning 'cause, because of, to rely on.'
田 (here representing round fruit, not its usual meaning 'field') — 果 pictures fruit hanging from branches.
木 (tree) — fruit growing on a tree gave 果 its meaning 'fruit' and, more broadly, 'result.'

example.hanzi: 科学家试图找出这两种现象之间的因果关系。
example.pinyin: Kēxuéjiā shìtú zhǎochū zhè liǎng zhǒng xiànxiàng zhījiān de yīnguǒ guānxì.
example.english: Scientists tried to determine the causal relationship between the two phenomena.
example.fact: One of statistics' most famous cautionary examples is the strong correlation between per-capita cheese consumption and deaths from becoming tangled in bedsheets in the U.S. — a textbook reminder that correlation alone never proves a causal relationship.

meanings: to take out and show to others

components.note: 屮 (a young sprout) growing up and out of 凵 (a container or pit) — a picture of something emerging, hence 'going out.'
A pictograph of an altar or offering table used in ancestor worship — presenting offerings extended to 示's meaning 'to show, display, indicate.'

example.hanzi: 请出示您的身份证件。
example.pinyin: Qǐng chūshì nín de shēnfèn zhèngjiàn.
example.english: Please show your identification.
example.fact: The modern passport photo requirement is a relatively recent convention — passports didn't commonly require photographs until World War I, when governments tightened border security and needed a fast way to visually verify identity.

components.note: 讠 (speech radical) — shows 说 relates to talking or language
兑 (duì) is the phonetic component; historically 说 was also pronounced closer to 兑's sound before shifting to shuō
口 (mouth) — 唱 describes singing, an action made with the mouth.
昌 (chāng) gives a sound close to chàng, differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 这位歌手擅长说唱和作曲。
example.pinyin: Zhè wèi gēshǒu shàncháng shuōchàng hé zuòqǔ.
example.english: This singer is skilled at rapping and composing.
example.fact: Hip-hop is generally traced to a specific date and place — August 11, 1973, at a back-to-school party in the Bronx, New York, where DJ Kool Herc extended the instrumental breaks of funk records, a technique that became the rhythmic foundation for rapping.

components.note: 纟 (silk/thread) — 经 originally referred to the vertical warp threads in weaving.
工 (gōng) gives a related sound cue for 经 (jīng), reflecting an older, closer pronunciation link between the two.
爫 (a hand, from above) — 受 pictures something being passed.
又 (a hand, from below) — one hand giving and another receiving gave 受 its meaning 'to receive' or 'to endure.'

example.hanzi: 这座桥经受住了强烈地震的考验。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò qiáo jīngshòu zhùle qiángliè dìzhèn de kǎoyàn.
example.english: This bridge withstood the test of a powerful earthquake.
example.fact: Modern base-isolated buildings, like Japan's Tokyo Skytree, are designed to withstand major earthquakes by sitting on flexible bearings or dampers that let the structure sway independently of violent ground motion, dramatically reducing the forces transmitted into the building itself.

components.note: 辶 (to walk) — 迷 originally described losing one's way while walking, extending to 'confused, obsessed.'
米 (mǐ) gives a sound distantly related to mí, having drifted apart over time.
亻 (person) plus 尔 (an old second-person pronoun) — combines to form 你, the modern word for 'you.'

example.hanzi: 她买了一辆迷你电动车。
example.pinyin: Tā mǎile yī liàng mínǐ diàndòngchē.
example.english: She bought a miniature electric car.
example.fact: The Mini Cooper, launched in 1959, was designed by Alec Issigonis largely in response to a 1956 fuel shortage — its transverse-mounted engine layout, unusual at the time, maximized interior space while keeping the car's footprint remarkably small, a layout most small cars still use today.

components.note: 里 (village, a unit of land) — 野 describes open country beyond the village.
予 (yǔ) reflects an older phonetic link, though the modern readings yě and yǔ have since diverged.
食 (food) — 餐 relates directly to eating and meals.

example.hanzi: 周末我们一家人去公园野餐。
example.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen yī jiā rén qù gōngyuán yěcān.
example.english: On the weekend, our family went to the park for a picnic.
example.fact: The modern picnic as an outdoor social meal became fashionable in France and Britain only after the French Revolution, when royal hunting grounds and parks that had been off-limits to commoners were opened to the public for the first time.

components.note: 禾 (grain) points to the harvest season.
火 (fire) recalls burning off crop stubble after harvest, giving 秋 its meaning 'autumn.'
大 (a person, arms outstretched) — represents a human being.
一 (a line, here representing the sky) — drawn above a person, showing what is above them: the heavens, hence 'sky, day.'

example.hanzi: 秋天的树叶渐渐变成了金黄色。
example.pinyin: Qiūtiān de shùyè jiànjiàn biànchéngle jīnhuángsè.
example.english: The autumn leaves gradually turned golden.
example.fact: Leaves turn color in autumn because trees stop producing chlorophyll, the green pigment that dominates through summer, unmasking yellow and orange carotenoid pigments that were present in the leaf all along but simply hidden.

components.note: 力 (strength) — relates to 办's meaning 'to handle, manage, do,' something accomplished through effort.
八 (bā) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from bàn.
至 (zhì, to arrive) — carries 到's core meaning, 'to reach, to arrive'
刂 (a form of 刀, dāo) gives a sound close to 到's pronunciation dào

example.hanzi: 这件事很难,但他最终办到了。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì hěn nán, dàn tā zuìzhōng bàndàole.
example.english: This was difficult, but he finally accomplished it.
example.fact: When Apollo 11 landed on the Moon in 1969, the onboard guidance computer had less processing power than a modern digital wristwatch, yet it still successfully guided the lunar module to a safe touchdown.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 探 describes reaching out with the hand to search for something.
戈 depicts a dagger-axe, a spear-like weapon with a blade jutting out to the side, pointing to the bottom-right.

example.hanzi: 他们在舞会上跳了一支探戈。
example.pinyin: Tāmen zài wǔhuì shàng tiàole yī zhī tàngē.
example.english: They danced a tango at the ball.
example.fact: The tango originated in the working-class port neighborhoods of Buenos Aires and Montevideo in the late 19th century, blending African, European, and South American musical influences — in 2009, UNESCO added it to the Intangible Cultural Heritage list.

components.note: 比 is made of two identical 匕 (spoon) shapes placed side by side — comparing two similar things led to its meaning 'to compare.'
方 likely depicts a plow with a square-edged blade, or two boats lashed side by side; either way the image of a squared, bounded shape gave 方 its meanings 'square, direction, method.'

example.hanzi: 打个比方,大脑就像一台超级计算机。
example.pinyin: Dǎ gè bǐfang, dànǎo jiù xiàng yī tái chāojí jìsuànjī.
example.english: To give an analogy, the brain is like a supercomputer.
example.fact: The human brain runs on roughly 20 watts of power, about what it takes to dimly light a lightbulb, yet performs pattern-recognition tasks that still outpace supercomputers requiring megawatts of electricity for comparable feats.

components.note: Now stands in for what was originally a piece of wood.
Represents notches cut into the wood to mark an agreement.
纟 (thread) — 约 originally meant 'to bind, tie up,' extending to 'to agree, arrange' and 'approximately.'

example.hanzi: 双方签订了一份正式契约。
example.pinyin: Shuāngfāng qiāndìngle yī fèn zhèngshì qìyuē.
example.english: Both parties signed a formal contract.
example.fact: Among the oldest known written contracts is a Sumerian clay tablet from around 2100 BCE recording a land sale, inscribed in cuneiform — a reminder that formal written agreements are almost as old as writing itself.

components.note: 辶 (to walk) — 进 relates to advancing or entering, both movement-related.
井 (jǐng) gives a close sound cue — 进 is pronounced jìn, sharing similar consonant and vowel sounds.
屮 (a young sprout) growing up and out of 凵 (a container or pit) — a picture of something emerging, hence 'going out.'

example.hanzi: 这个仓库每天有大量货物进出。
example.pinyin: Zhège cāngkù měitiān yǒu dàliàng huòwù jìnchū.
example.english: Large quantities of goods move in and out of this warehouse every day.
example.fact: The Port of Shanghai has been the world's busiest container port by volume every year since 2010, handling more than 47 million shipping containers in 2023 alone.

components.note: 尸 (a bent body shape) shows 屈 relates to bending.
出 (chū) gives a sound close to qū, sharing a similar consonant sound.
卩 (a person) — the one being dressed.
月 (a garment shape) — a hand 又 placing a coat on the person, giving 服 its meaning 'clothes; to obey, submit.'

example.hanzi: 面对压力,他始终没有屈服。
example.pinyin: Miànduì yālì, tā shǐzhōng méiyǒu qūfú.
example.english: Facing the pressure, he never gave in.
example.fact: During the 872-day Siege of Leningrad in World War II, the city's residents endured extreme famine and cold but never surrendered to the surrounding German forces, one of the longest and most destructive sieges in modern history.

components.note: 发 is a simplified form standing in for the traditional 發, which pictured legs launching an arrow from a bow — 'to shoot forth' broadened over time into 'to send out, to develop.'
犭 (dog) — 狂 originally described a mad, rabid dog, extending to 'wild, crazy.'
王 (wáng) gives a sound distantly related to kuáng, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 听到这个消息,她几乎要发狂了。
example.pinyin: Tīngdào zhège xiāoxi, tā jīhū yào fākuángle.
example.english: Hearing this news, she nearly went crazy.
example.fact: The 1518 Strasbourg dancing plague saw dozens of people reportedly dance uncontrollably in the streets for days, some until they collapsed from exhaustion — historians now suspect it was a case of mass psychogenic illness driven by extreme stress rather than any physical disease.

components.note: 土 (earth/soil) — 地's original meaning is 'earth, ground'
也 (yě) gives a partial sound match for 地's other reading dì; in this grammatical-particle usage the character is instead pronounced 'de'
辶 (to walk) — 道 relates to a path or road one walks along.
首 (shǒu) is the historical phonetic element; its modern reading no longer resembles dào, a reminder that sound components can drift after thousands of years of pronunciation change.

example.hanzi: 士兵们挖了一条地道逃出了监狱。
example.pinyin: Shìbīngmen wāle yī tiáo dìdào táochūle jiānyù.
example.english: The soldiers dug a tunnel and escaped from the prison.
example.fact: The Channel Tunnel connecting England and France runs 50 kilometers under the English Channel, of which 37 kilometers are undersea — making it the tunnel with the longest undersea section in the world.

components.note: 八 (to divide/split apart) — represents something already split into parts.
刀 (knife) — a knife cutting already-divided pieces further, giving 分 its meaning 'to divide, to separate.'

成 is traditionally read as a picture of a halberd or battle-axe, once used in the ceremony of striking an oath to seal an agreement — the act of finalizing something gave 成 its meaning 'to become, to complete, to succeed.'

example.hanzi: 老师把学生分成了四个小组。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī bǎ xuésheng fēnchéngle sì gè xiǎozǔ.
example.english: The teacher divided the students into four groups.
example.fact: A single fertilized human egg divides roughly 40 times over about nine months of gestation to become the trillions of cells that make up a newborn baby.

components.note: 尺 is traditionally read as a picture of a bent leg taking a measured step, used before rulers existed to pace off a distance — the origin of its meaning 'a Chinese foot, a ruler.'
寸 pictures a hand with a small mark near the wrist, showing the point about an inch up where a pulse can be felt — the image behind its meaning 'inch, small.'

example.hanzi: 请告诉我这件衣服的尺寸。
example.pinyin: Qǐng gàosu wǒ zhè jiàn yīfu de chǐcun.
example.english: Please tell me the size of this piece of clothing.
example.fact: The international standard meter was defined in 1799 as one ten-millionth of the distance from the North Pole to the equator; today it's defined instead by the distance light travels in a fraction of a second, a definition precise enough to be reproduced in any laboratory on Earth.

components.note: 车 (cart) — relates to 转's meaning 'to turn, change direction,' like a wheel turning.
专 (zhuān) gives a sound hint — 转 is pronounced zhuǎn, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.
宀 (a roof) sets the scene as a dwelling.
口 (an opening, here a window) lets light and air face outward — a house oriented a certain way gave 向 its meaning 'toward, direction.'

example.hanzi: 汽车突然转向,躲开了路上的障碍物。
example.pinyin: Qìchē tūrán zhuǎnxiàng, duǒkāile lù shàng de zhàng'àiwù.
example.english: The car suddenly changed direction to avoid the obstacle on the road.
example.fact: Modern car power steering systems can reduce the physical effort needed to turn the wheel by up to 80%, using hydraulic or electric assistance — a far cry from early automobiles, which sometimes required a driver's full upper-body strength to steer at low speed.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — 家 is about a home, the space under a roof.
豕 (shǐ, 'pig') supplies the ancient sound for 家; keeping a pig under one's roof was also a practical sign of a household in ancient China, though the modern readings jiā and shǐ no longer rhyme.
A vertical line 丨 running through the middle of a box or flag 口 — a simple image for the idea of 'center, middle.'

example.hanzi: 他大部分时间都待在家中。
example.pinyin: Tā dàbùfen shíjiān dōu dāizài jiāzhōng.
example.english: He spends most of his time at home.
example.fact: Studies of pre-industrial societies suggest people historically spent far more of their waking hours performing labor at or near their dwelling than modern urban office workers do — the sharp separation between 'home' and 'workplace' is largely a product of the last two centuries of industrialization.

components.note: 无 is a simplified form of 無, which originally pictured a person dancing while holding tufts of feathers or grain stalks in each hand; the dance-related meaning faded and the character was borrowed to write the negative 'not have, without.'
攵 (to strike) — 敌 relates to conflict and opposition, as with an enemy
啇 (dí) gives a sound close to 敌's reading dí

example.hanzi: 这支球队本赛季几乎无敌。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhī qiúduì běn sàijì jīhū wúdí.
example.english: This team has been nearly unbeatable this season.
example.fact: The Boston Celtics' 1985–86 NBA season included a 40–1 home record, one of the most dominant home-court performances in league history and a mark still cited as a benchmark for near invincibility.

components.note: 亻 (person) — relates to 传's meaning 'to pass on, transmit,' something passed from person to person.
专 (zhuān) gives a sound hint — 传 is pronounced chuán, sharing the same rhyme though the initial consonant differs.
直 (straight, upright) — 真 relates to something level and true.
几 (a small table) — an object placed level and true on a table gave 真 its meaning 'real' or 'true.'

example.hanzi: 请把合同用传真发给我们。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ hétong yòng chuánzhēn fāgěi wǒmen.
example.english: Please fax us the contract.
example.fact: The fax machine is far older than most people assume — Scottish inventor Alexander Bain patented an early fax-like device in 1843, decades before the telephone, using a pendulum-based scanning mechanism to transmit images over telegraph wires.

meanings: (of a relationship etc) to break down

components.note: 石 (rock/stone) — 破 relates to breaking, as a rock can be broken
皮 (pí) gives a loose sound connection to 破's reading pò
衣 (cloth) — 裂 describes cloth tearing apart.
列 (liè) is an exact match for the sound of 裂.

example.hanzi: 谈判在最后一刻破裂了。
example.pinyin: Tánpàn zài zuìhòu yī kè pòlièle.
example.english: The negotiations broke down at the last moment.
example.fact: The 1963 Vajont Dam disaster in Italy occurred not because the dam itself failed, but because a massive landslide into the reservoir sent a wave over the top of the dam — a reminder that structural failure in large infrastructure can come from the surrounding geology rather than the structure itself.

components.note: 弓 (bow) — a strong bow that took great force to draw gave 强 its meaning 'strong, powerful.'
虫 was a different phonetic element historically; its pronunciation has shifted so far from qiáng over time that the sound link is no longer obvious.
讠 (speech) — relates to 调's meaning 'to adjust, transfer,' something coordinated through spoken negotiation.
周 (zhōu) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from diào.

example.hanzi: 医生强调了充足睡眠的重要性。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng qiángdiàole chōngzú shuìmián de zhòngyàoxìng.
example.english: The doctor emphasized the importance of adequate sleep.
example.fact: The American researcher Randy Gardner's famous 1964 stint of staying awake for about 264 hours remains one of the most studied cases of extreme sleep deprivation on record, and it's part of why researchers now strongly discourage attempting to break such records.

meanings: (painting, embroidery etc) without following a model
(abbr. for 空手道[kong1 shou3 dao4]) karate

components.note: 穴 (a cave/hole) — 空 relates to an empty hollow space.
工 (gōng) gives a hint of the sound — 空 is pronounced kōng, a connection that has drifted over time.
手 is a simple picture of an open hand with the fingers spread out.

example.hanzi: 他空手夺下了对方的匕首。
example.pinyin: Tā kōngshǒu duóxiàle duìfāng de bǐshǒu.
example.english: He disarmed the opponent's dagger with his bare hands.
example.fact: Karate developed on the Ryukyu Islands, particularly Okinawa, partly as a response to a centuries-long ban on carrying weapons imposed by ruling authorities — practitioners trained empty-handed combat techniques that could be disguised within ordinary agricultural tool movements.

components.note: 臣 (a bowed eye, a person bending over) — depicts someone leaning down to look.
皿 (a basin of water) — before mirrors, people checked their reflection in a basin, giving 监 its meaning 'to observe, supervise, monitor.'
口 (mouth) — words spoken by a mouth are what reach the ear, giving 听 its meaning 'to listen.'
斤 stands in for the ear in this simplified character — the target that spoken words reach.

example.hanzi: 政府部门被指控监听公民的电话。
example.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ bùmén bèi zhǐkòng jiāntīng gōngmín de diànhuà.
example.english: The government department was accused of wiretapping citizens' phone calls.
example.fact: The 1972 Watergate break-in, in which operatives tied to President Nixon's re-election campaign attempted to wiretap the Democratic National Committee's offices, is one of the most consequential eavesdropping operations in American political history.

components.note: 冂 (a covering or frame, here representing a cart) — 两 pictures two things sharing one enclosure.
从 (two people following each other) — together with the frame above, 两 shows a pair joined together, giving its meaning 'two' or 'both.'
辶 (walking/movement) — links 边's meaning to a boundary or edge one moves along.
臱 (biān) gives the sound — 边 is also pronounced biān, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 街道两边种满了樱花树。
example.pinyin: Jiēdào liǎngbiān zhòngmǎnle yīnghuā shù.
example.english: Both sides of the street were lined with cherry blossom trees.
example.fact: Washington, D.C.'s famous cherry trees, planted along the Tidal Basin starting in 1912, were a gift from the city of Tokyo, and the annual bloom now draws over a million visitors each spring to see roughly 3,800 trees flower for just one to two weeks.

components.note: 大 (big) — 奖 describes something given as a big reward.
丬 (qiáng) gives a sound close to jiǎng.
木 (wood) — 杯 names a cup, originally carved from wood.
不 (bù) shares the initial b- with bēi, though the rhyme has drifted from ù to ēi over time.

example.hanzi: 冠军队举起了金色的奖杯。
example.pinyin: Guànjūn duì jǔqǐle jīnsè de jiǎngbēi.
example.english: The champion team lifted the golden trophy.
example.fact: The FIFA World Cup trophy, awarded since 1974, is made of 18-karat gold and weighs about 6.1 kilograms — winning teams don't actually keep the original trophy but receive a gold-plated replica instead, since the real one is returned to FIFA after the ceremony.

components.note: 羊 (sheep; here representing feathers or ornaments on a headdress) — an elaborate decoration worn on the head.
大 (a person, arms outstretched) — a person wearing a decorated headdress was seen as beautiful, giving 美 its meaning 'beautiful.'
林 here depicts eyes shut in sleep, not its usual meaning 'forest.'
夕 (evening, night) — sleeping at night is when dreams occur, giving 梦 its meaning 'dream.'

example.hanzi: 祝你今晚做个美梦。
example.pinyin: Zhù nǐ jīnwǎn zuò gè měimèng.
example.english: I wish you a beautiful dream tonight.
example.fact: Most vivid dreaming occurs during REM sleep, a stage the body enters roughly every 90 minutes throughout the night — during REM, the brain becomes almost as active as when awake, even though most voluntary muscles are temporarily paralyzed, a state that likely prevents sleepers from acting out their dreams.
